subject: Renewal conversation: consumption transition + temporary usage floor
messages:
From: Emma Carter <emma.carter@oxbridge.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal & mid-year growth — consumption transition?

Hi Ben,

Hope you had a good long weekend. Quick note from procurement and our engineering lead — we expect Oxbridge usage to ramp materially in Q3 (attached forecast) and we'd like to discuss options for the upcoming renewal. Two items in particular:

1) Move part of the mid-contract growth to a consumption-based top-up (we want the flexibility to burst without committing to a full uplift).
2) A temporary usage floor for the remainder of the contract so we don't see dramatic price volatility while we stabilize load.

From our side the procurement timeline is tight — aiming to have commercial terms signed by ~June 15 so we can align invoicing. Can you share a couple of concrete options (pricing bands, any short-term floor, and how co-terming would work if we convert to a consumption model)?

Attaching our internal usage forecast for Q3. Happy to set up a short call this week.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Carter
VP, Cloud Platform
Oxbridge AI
[Attachment: forecast_q3.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Carter <emma.carter@oxbridge.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & mid-year growth — consumption transition?

Thanks for the forecast, Emma — appreciate the heads up. Quick read-through and a couple of options that map to what you described. High-level first, then I can put a formal one-page appendix to the contract.

Option 1 — Consumption Top-ups (recommended for variable burst):
- You continue on current committed baseline.
- Additional usage billed monthly at a tiered overage rate: 0-20% over baseline at list*0.90, 20-50% at list*0.82, >50% at list*0.75 (list = standard per-token rate for your model family).
- Temporary usage floor: for the next 6 months we can guarantee a floor = 60% of current committed baseline; any consumption below that floor will be credited back quarterly.
- No co-term change required; this sits as an addendum.

Option 2 — Short-term Pro-rated Uplift + Co-term to Dec 31, 2027:
- One-time uplift to committed units for remainder of term (pro-rated).
- We would apply a one-time voucher credit to offset the uplift if you prefer a lower near-term cash outlay.
- Price for uplifted units: blended rate (existing commitment rate for baseline + discounted rate for uplifted portion).

Trade-offs: Option 1 gives elasticity and cleaner economics for spiky usage; Option 2 simplifies billing and forecasting for your finance team.

Next steps: if you like Option 1, I can draft the addendum and loop in legal; if you prefer Option 2 we can model the exact uplift number you need and I’ll share a pro-forma. Also looping Naomi and Jonas for approvals on the temporary floor and commercial language.

Would you be free for a 30 min sync Thurs (June 3) 10:00am PT?

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Oxbridge ask — proposed concessions and approvals

Team — following up from the external thread (Emma + Olivia). They want flexibility for Q3 and a short decision window (procurement wants signed by 6/15). My proposed commercial concessions:

- Temporary usage floor = 60% of their current baseline for 6 months (credits applied quarterly for shortfall).
- Consumption top-up tiers as in my external note but cap the deep discount (>50%) exposure to a $45k per-quarter protection (protects us from runaway burst).
- One-time voucher credit of $40k that can be applied to Q3 invoices if they choose Option 2 instead.

Questions for approvals:
- Naomi — can CS accept the 60% floor operationally and handle the quarterly credit flow?
- Jonas — legal: any language you want to pre-clear for the floor + cap? We need a short addendum + signature.
- Tessa — finance: can we structure the voucher so it amortizes across the next two invoices if they ask (avoid revenue recognition churn)?

If everyone is OK I’ll send the formal proposal + DocuSign link by Friday. I want to avoid escalating to leadership unless we hit a major redline.

Thanks,
Ben
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: consumption top-up + temporary floor (proposal attached)

Emma / Olivia — thanks for the call on Thursday. Per our discussion I’m attaching a short commercial appendix that implements the consumption top-up approach with the temporary usage floor and the optional voucher (see attached). Highlights:

- Floor: 60% of current baseline for 6 months, quarterly reconciliation and credit for shortfall.
- Consumption tiers: 0-20% at 10% discount; 20-50% at 18% discount; >50% at 25% discount up to a quarterly cap of $45k (Redwood protects downside beyond that).
- Voucher: one-time $40k credit available if Oxbridge chooses to convert to a pro-rated uplift instead of consumption top-ups.
- Legal: short addendum attached; we can DocuSign tonight if procurement is ready.
